question: Must fixed-temperature softmax attention lose sharp selection as input size grows, and does an entropy-adaptive temperature provide a reliable practical remedy for sharp size generalisation?

key_findings.claim: The bounded-logit dispersion lemma is correct: at any fixed nonzero temperature, every softmax coefficient is Theta(1/n) when all logits remain between size-independent constants.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma 2.1 directly sandwiches each coefficient between exp((m-M)/theta)/n and exp((M-m)/theta)/n. This is a clean statement about a family of increasing-dimensional softmax inputs, but the size-independent logit bounds and fixed temperature are decisive premises rather than consequences of softmax alone.

key_findings.claim: Theorem 2.2 validly obtains uniform logit bounds for a narrow fixed-depth continuous architecture over compact inputs, but the manuscript's broader claim that modern softmax architectures cannot learn sharp functions does not follow from the theorem as stated.
key_findings.evidence: The proof propagates compactness through continuous token-wise maps and convex-combination attention layers, then bounds every query-key dot product independently of n. It assumes a fixed composition of continuous blocks, global softmax, fixed theta > 0, and finite vocabulary; compact continuous input sets would suffice. It proves that individual coefficients vanish, not that every residual Transformer output necessarily loses all information required by every sharp task.

anchors.section: Key Theoretical Result and novelty claim

key_findings.claim: Size-dependent logit or temperature scaling, unbounded positional bias, hard/local/sparse/unnormalised attention, growing depth or recurrence, and discontinuous components fall outside the theorem, so the title should not be read as an impossibility result for all attention-based size generalisation.
key_findings.evidence: The authors themselves list unnormalised, sigmoid, stick-breaking, selective, hard, local, and discontinuous alternatives as escapes. The theorem does not model positional encodings or an explicit unbounded size signal; either can invalidate its uniform-logit premise. Chiang and Cholak's log-n scaling is mentioned as a size-dependent remedy, demonstrating that the fixed-parameter premise is operationally important.

anchors.section: Appendix C, depth and residual qualifications

key_findings.claim: The claimed first rigorous proof of variable-size attention dispersion omits a direct theoretical predecessor: Hahn 2020 already proves length-dependent limits in which a single input symbol's influence decays in fixed-depth self-attention.
key_findings.evidence: The related-work section calls Yan et al. and Ebrahimi et al. empirical predecessors and says this paper is the first rigorous proof. Yet Michael Hahn's 2020 TACL paper, arXiv:1906.06755v2, establishes theoretical self-attention limitations including decreasing dependence on individual symbols. The manuscript cites Chiang and Cholak 2022, whose abstract explicitly frames its contribution as overcoming Hahn's lemma, but does not cite Hahn. This paper's compactness-to-bounded-logit formulation and sharp-function framing are useful refinements, not an uncontested first proof of the underlying dilution phenomenon.

key_findings.claim: The single-head maximum-retrieval experiment is a useful controlled demonstration of attention dispersion, but it validates only one synthetic architecture and data distribution.
key_findings.evidence: A one-head Deep-Sets-style model receives priorities sampled uniformly on [0,1] plus one of ten random classes, trains for 100,000 Adam steps on set sizes 5-16, and is evaluated through size 16,384. Its accuracy and visual attention sharpness degrade steadily with size, which aligns with the lemma. Continuous priority values technically differ from the theorem's finite vocabulary, although their compact support still permits a compactness argument for this fixed continuous network.

key_findings.claim: Entropy-adaptive temperature yields statistically detectable but modest and transient max-retrieval gains; it does not arrest asymptotic failure.
key_findings.evidence: Across ten seeds, baseline versus adaptive accuracy is 53.8% versus 57.7% at n=1,024, 22.6% versus 24.9% at n=4,096, and 12.4% versus 14.0% at n=16,384, close to the ten-class chance rate. The paper reports paired t-tests at each size but no correction across eleven comparisons or uncertainty intervals. At the training boundary n=16 both methods are 98.6%, and both collapse as size rises.

key_findings.claim: Entropy is insufficient to identify an optimal temperature, making the fitted inverse polynomial a task- and model-specific heuristic rather than a general adaptive rule.
key_findings.evidence: The method discards cases where the target already has the largest logit, grid-searches theta from 0 to 10 in 0.1 increments on wrong-argmax max-retrieval samples, and fits beta from entropy alone with a hand-set entropy threshold of 0.5 and beta floor of 1. Distinct logit vectors can have the same entropy but different target ranks and gaps, so they can require different temperatures; entropy is not a sufficient statistic for the target-aware optimum.

anchors.section: Appendix F, fit data, grid search, and thresholds

key_findings.claim: The CLRS-Text result is not evidence for an inference-time drop-in correction because that intervention failed; the reported improvement requires fine-tuning a modified model.
key_findings.evidence: The paper explicitly says applying the learned polynomial only at inference does not work on CLRS-Text. It then replaces softmax in every Gemma 2B attention head during both fine-tuning and inference, allowing the model to adapt its key/query embeddings. This changes the trained architecture and optimization path, so the comparison cannot isolate post-hoc temperature correction.

anchors.section: Section 4.2, failed inference-only transfer and fine-tuning intervention

key_findings.claim: CLRS-Text reporting is visually suggestive but too incomplete for a strong general algorithmic size-generalisation claim.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 8 shows performance profiles for thirty algorithms and the prose says adaptive temperature is better on nearly all tasks, with named outliers including Heapsort, MST Kruskal, and Bubble Sort. The paper gives no numerical result table, independent training-seed count, uncertainty intervals, complete fine-tuning hyperparameters, or correction for the thirty-task panel. A 2,048-token output cap also removes sizes whose answer does not fit.

key_findings.claim: Corollary B.1's finite-precision proof is invalid as written because machine epsilon is not a universal threshold below which a positive coefficient becomes numerically zero.
key_findings.evidence: The proof concludes that alpha < machine epsilon is indistinguishable from zero and therefore the weighted sum exactly reduces to the all-v_b representation. Machine epsilon is the spacing near 1, not the smallest positive normal or subnormal value and not a general accumulation-error threshold. A real-arithmetic argument could instead use continuity plus a nonzero classifier margin to show eventual label stability near the all-v_b point, but that repair is not the printed finite-precision proof.

anchors.section: Corollary B.1 proof and machine-epsilon step

key_findings.claim: Remark B.2 does not prove the claimed whole-Transformer misclassification result, especially with residual connections.
key_findings.evidence: The remark asserts that dispersed attention makes two deep-model embeddings indistinguishable and says residual-preserved information cannot later be integrated. Individual O(1/n) head weights do not establish identical residual streams or identical final logits, and in the GPT sketch v_a is placed at the final position, whose residual path can preserve it directly. Appendix C later concedes that the clean propagation argument does not apply with residuals or GPT-style attention because representations can be re-amplified.

anchors.section: Appendix C, residual and GPT qualification

key_findings.claim: Gemma entropy curves show correlation with input length, not that softmax dispersion causally explains the model's errors or that the identified heads implement the relevant computation.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 visualises first-block head entropy on a maximum prompt as sequence length varies. The authors explicitly decline the mechanistic work needed to identify relevant head behavior or establish that robustness depends on those heads. Consequently the observation supports a descriptive attention statistic, not a causal failure diagnosis.

key_findings.claim: The streaming entropy derivation preserves linear memory, but the implementation claim is not an efficiency benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix G derives cumulative normalizer and logit-weighted-sum updates and reports numerical agreement plus contexts up to 131,072 tokens on one A100. The authors explicitly say the algorithm is not FLOP-efficient, while the main implementation performs two softmax calls and extra tensor operations. No latency, throughput, FLOP, kernel, memory-peak, or end-to-end quality-versus-cost comparison with FlashAttention is reported.

anchors.section: Appendix G, streaming setup and 131,072-token test

key_findings.claim: The authors appropriately acknowledge that adaptive temperature is ad hoc and does not escape the fixed-temperature theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion says the method only holds dispersion at bay to a certain extent and explicitly states that it does not escape the theory. The strongest supported takeaway is therefore a bounded-logit diagnostic and motivation to compare alternative attention normalisations, not a solved length-generalisation mechanism.

method.core_idea: Prove that fixed-temperature softmax with uniformly bounded logits assigns vanishing mass to every individual item as set size grows, lift the bound to a compact fixed-depth Transformer model, and heuristically sharpen attention by mapping observed entropy to a lower temperature.
method.mechanism: Compactness of the representation spaces bounds all query-key logits, allowing a 1/n coefficient sandwich. Empirically, a single-head max-retrieval network is trained only on small sets and tested on much larger ones. For mitigation, the original softmax entropy is passed through a fitted degree-four inverse polynomial to obtain beta, subject to a low-entropy gate and beta floor; softmax is then recomputed on beta-scaled logits. The same mechanism is trained into all heads of Gemma 2B for CLRS-Text.
assumptions: The architecture has fixed depth and fixed parameters as n grows.
Inputs live in a finite or otherwise compact set and all per-token transformations are continuous.
Attention is global, softmax-normalised, and uses a fixed strictly positive temperature in the theorem.
No unbounded position, distance, or explicit size signal makes the logit spread grow with n.
Decay of each individual attention coefficient is sufficient to diagnose loss of the task-relevant sharp computation.
Softmax entropy alone contains enough information to choose a useful target-aware temperature.
A polynomial fitted on one max-retrieval model transfers to all heads and tasks after suitable fine-tuning.
The synthetic max-retrieval and CLRS-Text results are informative about robust reasoning circuits in larger contemporary models.

techniques.role: Bounds every softmax coefficient above and below by constants times 1/n.
Propagates compact representation spaces through continuous MLPs and convex-combination attention to obtain size-independent logit bounds.
Provides a controlled variable-set-size task in which attention should select the largest-priority item.
Fits a degree-four inverse polynomial from softmax entropy to a lower proposed temperature.
Grid-searches temperatures on wrong-argmax samples to maximise the ground-truth item's probability before fitting the heuristic.
Computes baseline probabilities and entropy, gates sharpening below entropy 0.5, floors beta at one, and recomputes softmax.
Replaces every Gemma 2B attention softmax during fine-tuning and inference on thirty algorithmic tasks.
Updates the softmax normalizer and a logit-weighted cumulative term without materialising the quadratic attention matrix.

evaluations.setting: One-head set-attention classifier trained for 100,000 steps on max-retrieval sets of size 5-16 and evaluated through size 16,384 over ten seeds.
evaluations.metric: Class accuracy, attention maps, logit spread, and paired t-test p-values at each size.
evaluations.result: Baseline accuracy falls from 98.6% at size 16 to 12.4% at 16,384; adaptive temperature reaches 14.0% at 16,384 and modestly improves intermediate sizes but does not prevent collapse.
evaluations.baseline: The identical trained model using standard fixed-temperature softmax at inference.

evaluations.setting: Gemma 2B first-block attention heads prompted to find a maximum as the number of listed items increases.
evaluations.metric: Shannon entropy of each attention head.
evaluations.result: Head entropy rises with input size in the displayed prompt, consistent with dispersion, but no causal link to prediction failures or head function is established.
evaluations.baseline: The same frozen model and prompt family at shorter input lengths.

evaluations.setting: Gemma 2B fine-tuned on all thirty CLRS-Text algorithmic execution tasks with or without adaptive temperature in every head.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy profiles across in- and out-of-distribution problem sizes, shown graphically.
evaluations.result: The adaptive model is visually better on nearly all tasks but has outliers; no numerical table, uncertainty, or training-seed replication is supplied, and inference-only transfer is reported to fail.
evaluations.baseline: A separately fine-tuned standard-softmax Gemma 2B under incompletely reported training details.

evaluations.setting: Streaming entropy implementation at context lengths up to 131,072 tokens on a single NVIDIA A100.
evaluations.metric: Numerical agreement of temperature outputs and ability to execute at long context under linear memory.
evaluations.result: The authors report matching outputs and successful execution, but provide no speed, FLOP, peak-memory, or end-to-end performance benchmark.
evaluations.baseline: Naive entropy materialisation and conceptual compatibility with FlashAttention rather than a measured optimized-kernel baseline.

limitations: Author-stated: adaptive temperature is ad hoc, only delays dispersion, and does not escape the theorem.
Author-stated: applying the fitted rule only at inference fails on CLRS-Text, requiring fine-tuning with the modified attention.
Author-stated: mechanistic attribution of relevant Gemma heads and causal dependence on their entropy is outside scope.

Reviewer-identified: the theorem requires size-independent bounded logits, fixed depth and parameters, continuous compact representations, global softmax, and fixed positive temperature; several common and proposed architectures fall outside it.
Reviewer-identified: vanishing individual attention weights do not alone prove an impossibility for every residual Transformer computation of every sharp function.
Reviewer-identified: Hahn 2020 is an omitted direct theoretical predecessor, substantially weakening the first-proof novelty claim.
Reviewer-identified: Corollary B.1 misuses machine epsilon, and Remark B.2 does not establish the residual/deep case.
Reviewer-identified: the entropy-to-temperature fit is non-identifiable from entropy alone and is calibrated on a selected subset from one synthetic model.
Reviewer-identified: CLRS-Text lacks numerical tables, full hyperparameters, training-seed uncertainty, and a clean inference-only intervention.
Reviewer-identified: the max-retrieval improvements are small, are tested with many uncorrected p-values, and decay toward chance at the largest sizes.
Reviewer-identified: no policy-size, model-size, task-family, vocabulary, positional-encoding, or explicit logit-scaling ablation maps the theorem's practical boundary.
Reviewer-identified: the streaming implementation is not compared on latency, throughput, FLOPs, kernel efficiency, or memory peak.
failure_modes: A fixed logit spread makes all attention weights O(1/n), degrading retrieval when downstream computation needs a non-vanishing contribution from one item.
Lowering temperature sharpens the wrong argmax and can make an already incorrect attention decision more confident.
Two heads with equal entropy but different target ranks or logit gaps receive the same beta despite requiring different corrections.
The fitted polynomial extrapolates outside the entropy and context regime used for max-retrieval calibration.
Inference-time attention replacement shifts hidden-state distributions in a pretrained model and fails without retraining.
Training with adaptive temperature learns around the intervention, confounding claims that the rule itself caused size generalisation.
Unbounded relative-position biases or explicit size signals violate the bounded-logit premise and produce behavior the theorem does not predict.
Residual paths retain a decisive token even when attention weights disperse, invalidating a naive whole-network impossibility inference.
Finite-precision arguments based on machine epsilon predict numerical erasure at the wrong scale.
The second softmax and entropy bookkeeping preserve asymptotic memory while imposing enough compute overhead to erase practical long-context benefits.
reusable_insights: Any claim about softmax length failure should report how the logit spread and temperature scale with n, not only attention entropy.
A clean theorem boundary can become an experimental checklist: compactness, continuity, positional signals, fixed depth, global normalization, and size-dependent parameters should each be ablated.
Attention-weight dilution and end-to-end task impossibility are separate claims; the latter needs a margin, sensitivity, or information-flow argument through residual computation.
Adaptive normalization should condition on target-free distribution shape richer than a scalar entropy, and its calibration must be held out across heads, tasks, lengths, and models.
Inference-only, continued-pretraining, and from-scratch interventions answer different questions and should be reported separately.
A numerically meaningful failure threshold should use the actual floating-point operation, exponent range, accumulator precision, and classifier margin rather than machine epsilon alone.
Alternative normalizers should be compared at matched parameter count, training tokens, kernel maturity, memory, throughput, and length distribution.
open_questions: Can the coefficient lemma be lifted to a rigorous residual-Transformer task lower bound using a quantified output margin or token-influence norm?
Which deployed positional encodings or relative biases make the logit spread grow with length, and at what rate do they evade or merely postpone dispersion?
Does a target-free statistic using entropy, top-logit gap, effective support, kurtosis, and head role select temperature more reliably than entropy alone?
How do adaptive temperature, log-n scaling, sparsemax, sigmoid, selective attention, stick-breaking, and SSMax compare under one matched long-context training and kernel benchmark?
Can a post-hoc calibration rule improve CLRS-Text without fine-tuning, or is architectural adaptation during training necessary?
What training-size and model-size scaling law predicts the length at which retrieval accuracy begins to collapse?
Do causal head ablations confirm that rising entropy in the measured heads mediates the observed reasoning error?
What is the wall-clock and energy frontier of streaming entropy once fused into a production-quality FlashAttention-style kernel?

competitive_landscape.title: Theoretical Limitations of Self-Attention in Neural Sequence Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Hahn proves fixed-depth self-attention limitations including decay of dependence on individual input symbols and formal-language failures. The present paper gives a simpler compactness-to-bounded-logit statement and sharp-function framing, but its claim to the first rigorous variable-length dispersion proof does not account for this predecessor.

competitive_landscape.title: Overcoming a Theoretical Limitation of Self-Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Chiang and Cholak explicitly build on Hahn and show constructions plus a simple attention-scaling remedy for length generalisation. Their scaling depends on length, whereas this paper fits a content-entropy-dependent temperature under a fixed-temperature impossibility theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers need glasses! Information over-squashing in language tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: closely related theory from overlapping authors
competitive_landscape.difference: This predecessor analyzes decoder-only representation collapse and token-sensitivity decay, including low-precision effects. The present work isolates softmax coefficient dispersion through bounded logits and proposes adaptive temperature, but inherits the need to separate head-level dilution from full-model failure.

competitive_landscape.title: Your Context Is Not an Array: Unveiling Random Access Limitations in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Ebrahimi et al. connect parity length-generalisation failures to random access and visualize where attention fails, with content addressing as a workaround. The present paper supplies a general bounded-logit coefficient lemma but tests an entropy-based sharpening heuristic rather than random-access mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.title: From Softmax to Sparsemax: A Sparse Model of Attention and Multi-Label Classification
competitive_landscape.difference: Sparsemax projects onto the simplex and can assign exact zero mass to irrelevant items, directly escaping dense softmax dilution. It predates the present adaptive-temperature heuristic but was not designed or evaluated as a modern large-model length-generalisation solution.

competitive_landscape.title: Theory, Analysis, and Best Practices for Sigmoid Self-Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Sigmoid attention removes global probability normalization, proves universal approximation and regularity properties, and supplies a hardware-aware kernel plus multimodal experiments. It escapes the coefficient-sum mechanism rather than dynamically sharpening two softmax calls.

competitive_landscape.title: Selective Attention Improves Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: Selective Attention removes unneeded context with a parameter-free attention modification and reports language-model quality plus large KV-memory reductions. It attacks dilution by shrinking the effective context, while the present method retains every token and changes temperature from entropy.

competitive_landscape.title: Differential Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: Differential attention subtracts two softmax maps to suppress irrelevant context and reports long-context and retrieval gains. Because each constituent map remains normalized, the present paper correctly notes that subtraction may not evade asymptotic dispersion, although it can improve finite-length selectivity.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Stick-Breaking Attention: An Efficient Implementation and In-depth Study
competitive_landscape.difference: Stick-breaking attention allocates probability sequentially with an intrinsic recency bias and supplies an efficient implementation with extrapolation from 2^11 to 2^14 context. It changes normalization and ordering assumptions rather than fitting a scalar temperature to entropy.

competitive_landscape.title: Scalable-Softmax Is Superior for Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: SSMax directly scales softmax with input size and reports benefits when used from pretraining as well as during or after pretraining. It is a simpler length-conditioned response to the same flattening problem and should be a central baseline for future adaptive-temperature evaluation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first rigorous proof that softmax attention necessarily disperses as the number of logits grows, uses it to argue that modern softmax architectures cannot robustly sustain sharp reasoning circuits, and proposes entropy-adaptive temperature as a practical mitigation.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its distinctive contribution is the concise bounded-logit 1/n lemma, a compactness lift to a class of fixed-depth continuous Transformer graphs, and a fitted entropy-to-temperature heuristic tested on max retrieval and CLRS-Text.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The coefficient lemma and compactness proof are clear and reusable, but the first-proof claim is materially weakened by omitted direct prior work from Hahn 2020, and the whole-Transformer impossibility extension is not proven for residual architectures. The empirical mitigation is a task-specific heuristic with modest synthetic gains and a fine-tuning-confounded CLRS result. The supportable novelty is therefore a useful reformulation and diagnostic plus an exploratory intervention, not a general impossibility theorem or validated solution to sharp size generalisation.
